        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Kapteyn 5 Belt: BlkBeard, one dark punctuation     │
        │ Alrakis Commerce Vein: profit with ice in its jaw  │
        │ Ross 614 Black Vein: the mine calls itself nature  │
        │ Furud Legacy Drift: even debris wants a monument   │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

The planet wore its name like a sentence too long for one mouth: Fumalsamakah I.
Above it, the Spent Crucible hung like an emptied factory bowl, still warm with the idea of extraction.
The Frost Ring kept circling anyway, loyal as a worker paid in scenery.
I thought of Graffias, where Trade Crystal Shard Field glittered under the indifferent eyes of Madonna, Wexler Q75-M5, and Wexler X9W-AE, and how every jewel in space is just a wound taught to sparkle.
I thought of Frontier, where I went looking for Scout Docks and found only Icecap Drift, Old Survey Station, Veil Nebula, and the administrative shrug of absence.
Kapteyn 5 had BlkBeard drifting near the Weak Annihilation Zone like a rumor that learned to pilot.
Alrakis named its asteroid belt Commerce Vein with the honesty of a knife.
Ross 614 offered a Black Vein and a Fading Ember, as if industry and exhaustion were twin gods sharing one furnace.
In Furud, Vapor Fields blurred the edges of memory while Legacy Drift insisted trash can inherit empire.
Saltwind had a Gas Pocket and an ENDL station, proof that even the most lyrical weather gets filed.
Gliese 229 kept only a Star and a Haze, which felt almost merciful.
Yed Prior stacked Belt, Emission Nebula, and Cryobelt like a sermon on accumulation.
Kepler-442 glowed cleanly, still pretending stars are innocent.
And here at Fumalsamakah, the crucible is called spent, but the orbit says otherwise.
Everything still turns.
Everything still gets counted.
Even beauty arrives itemized, in belts and fields and veins, until some fool looks up and mistakes the ledger for a sky.
